extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants (patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for when and how material may be incorporated by reference into U.S. patent applications and related requirements for specifications (including substitute specifications, corrections, and presentation of examples). Covers what is 'essential' vs 'nonessential', permitted source documents, correction procedures, timing, and formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding inadvertently omitted material under 37 CFR 1.57(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.57(b) permits inadvertently omitted material to be added to the application by way of a later filed amendment if the inadvertently omitted portion of the specification or drawing(s) is completely contained in a prior-filed application (for which priority/benefit is claimed) even though there is no explicit incorporation by reference of the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §217 for discussion regarding 37 CFR 1.57(b). This provides a procedure (created by PLTIA implementation) to add omitted material when it is fully contained in a prior-filed application for which priority/benefit is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing a nonprovisional by reference under 35 U.S.C. 111(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: As provided in 35 U.S.C. 111(c), as amended by PLTIA, a nonprovisional application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after December 18, 2013, may be filed by a reference to a previously filed application indicating that the specification and any drawings of the application are replaced by the reference to the previously filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §601.01(a), subsection III, for information on conditions (including payment of a surcharge) under which such a reference shall constitute the specification and any drawings of the subsequent application for purposes of a filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference policy for applications to issue as U.S. patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's incorporation by reference practice with respect to applications which issue as U.S. patents provides the public with a patent disclosure which minimizes the public’s burden to search for and obtain copies of documents incorporated by reference which may not be readily available. The Director has elected to exercise discretion in a specified manner (guidance in Section A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy ensures reasonably complete disclosures are published as U.S. patents; guidance differs for applications that are relied on only to establish earlier effective filing dates (Section B). See MPEP §608.01 for details and MPEP §2181 for impact on 35 U.S.C.112(b)/112(f) issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'essential material' (37 CFR 1.57(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: “Essential material” is material necessary to (1) provide a written description and enablement (35 U.S.C.112(a)), (2) describe the claimed invention in terms that particularly point out and distinctly claim it (35 U.S.C.112(b)), or (3) describe structure/material/acts corresponding to a claimed means or step (35 U.S.C.112(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In any application that is to issue as a U.S. patent, essential material may only be incorporated by reference to a U.S. patent or patent application publication. Material meeting any of these statutory requirements is treated as essential and cannot properly be incorporated from improper sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonessential subject matter and permissible sources (37 CFR 1.57(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonessential subject matter is subject matter referred to for indicating background or illustrating state of the art; it may be incorporated by reference to patents or applications published by the United States or foreign/regional patent offices, prior and concurrently filed commonly owned U.S. applications, or non-patent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonessential material is less restricted than essential material; reliance on commonly-assigned or copending applications for nonessential material is ordinarily permitted. See 37 CFR 1.57(e) and cited cases (In re Fried; General Electric Co. v. Brenner).

rubrics_metrics.name: No incorporation by hyperlink or browser-executable code
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference by hyperlink or other form of browser executable code is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.57(e) and MPEP §608.01. Hyperlinks do not constitute acceptable incorporation by reference into the specification for the purposes of disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for 'incorporated by reference' root words (37 CFR 1.57(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper incorporation by reference (except as provided in 37 CFR 1.57(b)) is limited to instances where the perfecting words 'incorporated by reference' or the root words (e.g., incorporating, incorporated) and 'reference' (e.g., referencing) appear in the referencing statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The root-word requirement provides a bright-line test; references not meeting it will be treated as noncompliant and may require correction per 37 CFR 1.57(h). If intent to incorporate is not clearly indicated, examination proceeds as if no incorporation was made and the Office will not expend resources assuming incorporation was intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and specific portion citation requirement (37 CFR 1.57(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The referencing application must include an identification of the referenced patent, application, or publication, and particular attention should be directed to specific portions of the referenced document where subject matter being incorporated may be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application leaves application number blanks or provides insufficient identification, guidelines (e.g., In re Fouche) address filling such items; correction that uniquely identifies the document may be permitted under 1.57(h)(2). Examiners should require specific identification when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation/substitution of essential material when complete disclosure filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is filed with a complete disclosure, essential material may be canceled by amendment and substituted by reference to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication. The amendment must be accompanied by a statement signed by the applicant or practitioner stating the material canceled is the same material incorporated by reference and no new matter has been included (37 CFR 1.57(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same procedure is available for nonessential material. Careful compliance with the signed statement requirement is necessary to avoid introducing new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require copy of incorporated material (37 CFR 1.57(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application as filed incorporates material by reference, a copy of the incorporated material may be required to be submitted to the Office even if properly incorporated by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include examiner review, putting material in context, or where the material is being inserted by amendment in lieu of an improper incorporation. If required, the copy must be accompanied by a statement that it is the same material incorporated by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper incorporation and correction limitations (37 CFR 1.57(g) and (h))
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation of essential material to an unpublished U.S. patent application, a foreign application or patent, or to a publication is improper under 37 CFR 1.57(d). A previously noncompliant incorporation by reference statement may be corrected by an amendment (37 CFR 1.57(g)), but the amendment must not include new matter. Noncompliant incorporations must be corrected within the time period set by the Office and no later than the close of prosecution or abandonment (37 CFR 1.57(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until corrected, underlying objections or rejections (e.g., under 35 U.S.C.112) should be made by the examiner. Improper incorporations and late corrections waste examination resources and can slow prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(h)(1) — correction when clear intent to incorporate exists
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.57(h)(1) authorizes correction of noncompliant incorporation statements that omit the root words if the application as filed clearly conveys an intent to incorporate the material by reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider the language used, context, and any additional arguments or evidence. Examples include sequence identification by database accession numbers where intent is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.57(h)(2) — correction when document can be uniquely identified
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.57(h)(2) allows correction of a citation where the document is sufficiently described to uniquely identify it. Correction that results in identification that cannot be determined from the original citation may constitute new matter and is not authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of impermissible correction: citation originally points to an unrelated book with no other identifying info — cannot replace with intended journal article because original citation does not permit identification. Attorney docket numbers etc. may suffice but specifying application number is preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate corrective avenues (no 1.183 petition; use revive/reissue where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to suspend the time period requirement in 37 CFR 1.57(h) is not appropriate. After abandonment applicant must file a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137; after issuance, corrections may require reissue. Correcting via certificate of correction is not appropriate because it may alter claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections that would alter claim scope should be made via the reissue process. Reliance on 1.183 is unlikely to succeed; selection of the appropriate corrective mechanism is required depending on stage (abandonment, issuance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of applicant amendments that change essentiality of incorporated material (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files an amendment (e.g., adding a limitation) that makes previously-incorporated material essential, an examiner may require the applicant to amend the specification to include that material and may make rejections under 35 U.S.C.112(a) if the material is not included. Correction must comply with 37 CFR 1.57(g) and timing rules; applicant may also file an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 with appropriate fee and amend under 1.57(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given: (1) examiner notices specification incorporated essential material from a foreign patent and requires amendment to add material; (2) applicant adds claim limitation supported only by foreign patent making the incorporated subject matter essential, leading to a 112(a) rejection in final Office action. If rejection results from applicant amendment, finality of action is proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs for office communications (¶6.19, ¶6.19.01, ¶6.19.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs are provided for common examiner communications regarding incorporation by reference: e.g., ¶6.19 Incorporation by Reference, Unpublished U.S. Application, Foreign Patent or Application, Publication; ¶6.19.01 Ineffective Incorporation by Reference, General; ¶6.19.03 Correction of Ineffective Incorporation by Reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs specify how to identify the document and reasons for ineffectiveness, and explain required applicant responses/timing and statements per 37 CFR 1.57(g). Examiners are advised what to include in bracketed fields and follow-on paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date consequences of corrections to incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of any application wherein essential material is improperly incorporated by reference will not be affected by applicant’s correction where (A) there is a clear intent to incorporate by reference the intended material and the correction is to add the root words, (B) the incorporated document can be uniquely identified and the correction clarifies identification, and (C) the correction inserts material from the reference where incorporation is to an unpublished U.S. patent application, foreign application or patent, or to a publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where these conditions are not met, correction may affect the filing date; examiners and applicants should carefully evaluate corrections relative to filing-date consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on commonly-assigned/copending applications for nonessential material
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on a commonly-assigned, prior filed or concurrently filed copending application may ordinarily be made to complete the disclosure provided the incorporated material is directed to nonessential material (see 37 CFR 1.57(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: In re Fried; General Electric Co. v. Brenner. This is an ordinary practice for background/nonessential information but not for essential material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot rely on subsequent publications or later-filed applications for filing-date disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Since a disclosure must be complete as of the filing date, subsequent publications or subsequently filed applications cannot be relied on to establish a constructive reduction to practice or an enabling disclosure as of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: White Consol. Indus. v. Vega Servo-Control; In re Scarbrough; In re Glass. Applicants must ensure the filing contains the enabling disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of incorporation-by-reference statement at filing to safeguard benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may include a statement at the time of filing the later application incorporating by reference the prior application as a safeguard against omission of a portion of a prior application for which priority/benefit is claimed. The incorporation-by-reference statement must be filed at the time of filing the later-filed application to be effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incorporation statement added after filing is not effective because no new matter may be added after filing (35 U.S.C.132(a)). Note: such a statement will not satisfy the specific reference requirement of 35 U.S.C.119(e) or 120 or 37 CFR 1.78. See MPEP §§201.06(c), 211 et seq., 213–216, and 217.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper presentation of simulated/predicted test results and prophetic (paper) examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulated or predicted test results and prophetic examples are permitted. Working examples correspond to work actually performed; paper examples describe embodiments not actually conducted. Paper examples should not be represented as work actually done, and no results should be represented as actual unless they have actually been achieved. Paper examples should not be described using the past tense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hoffman-La Roche v. Promega and 'Properly Presenting Prophetic and Working Examples in a Patent Application,' 86 FR 35074 (July 1, 2021) for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When the Office may require a substitute specification (37 CFR 1.125(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number or nature of the amendments or the legibility of the application papers renders it difficult to consider the application, or to arrange the papers for printing or copying, the Office may require the entire specification, including the claims, or any part thereof, be rewritten (37 CFR 1.125(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legibility includes ability to be photocopied/scanned for electronic reproduction. Form paragraph 6.28 may be used where the specification is in faulty English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary substitute specification filing and limits (37 CFR 1.125(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to §1.312, a substitute specification, excluding the claims, may be filed at any point up to payment of the issue fee if it is accompanied by a statement that the substitute specification includes no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification voluntarily filed will be accepted if requirements of 1.125(b) are satisfied. A substitute specification is not permitted in a reissue application or in a reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.125(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and marking requirements for substitute specifications (37 CFR 1.125(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification submitted must be accompanied by markings showing all changes relative to the immediate prior version of the specification of record. Added subject matter must be shown by underlining; deleted matter by strike-through or double brackets as specified. An accompanying clean version must also be supplied. Paragraph numbering of the specification of record is not considered a change for marking purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs of any substitute specification (other than claims) should be individually numbered in Arabic numerals (e.g., [0001]) to permit replacement paragraphs under 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1). The substitute must be submitted in clean form without markings and with a marked-up copy showing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties and limitations regarding substitute specifications (no duty to detailed-compare)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no obligation on the examiner to make a detailed comparison between the old and new specifications to determine whether new matter has been added. If, however, an examiner becomes aware that new matter is present, an objection should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification which complies should normally be entered; if denied entry, form paragraph 6.28.02 may be used to notify applicant of reasons (e.g., missing no-new-matter statement, missing marked copy, filed in reissue, filed after payment of issue fee, containing claims). See MPEP §714.20 regarding entry of amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of idiomatic English (¶6.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification in proper idiomatic English and in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b) is required where the specification's English is faulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The substitute specification filed must be accompanied by a statement that it contains no new matter. Use form paragraph 6.28 where the examiner requires a new specification for faulty English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of canceled matter (37 CFR 1.121)
rubrics_metrics.description: Canceled text in the specification can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously canceled matter as a new insertion (37 CFR 1.121(b)(4)). A claim canceled by amendment may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number (37 CFR 1.121(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §714 for details on reinstatement procedures; canceled matter is not simply restored without presenting it as new subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use/transfer of specification or drawings in subsequent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No part of a specification can normally be transferred to another application. Similarly, drawings cannot normally be transferred to another application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §608.02(i) for exceptions and further guidance; the general rule is that transfer is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derogatory remarks about prior art are prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may refer to the general state of the art and the advance made by the invention, but is not permitted to make derogatory or disparaging statements concerning the products or processes of any particular person other than the applicant; mere comparisons with the prior art are not considered disparaging per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid statements disparaging other persons' inventions, patents, or products in the specification. Keep comparisons factual and focused on the invention's advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use of marks, trade names, and trademarks in patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and guidance on 'trade name', 'commercial name', 'mark', 'trademark', and 'service mark' are provided (15 U.S.C.1127 and related text) describing when such terms are relevant and how marks may be construed in patent documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §608.01(v) for details on treatment of trademarks and trade names and problems arising from designation of materials by trademark/trade name (see MPEP §608.01(v) cross-reference).
